ranking_table.title: Opportunity #1: Combining Multiple Details (Person + Place + Time)
ranking_table.what_it_means: While Google Photos promises natural multi-detail search, in practice combining more than one clue (like person, place, and time) often returns zero results or ignores key words.
ranking_table.why_it_is_important: Because Google tells users this works, expectations are high. When combining basic clues fails, users lose trust in the search bar and give up.

ranking_table.title: Opportunity #2: Natural-Language Questions Misread by Ask Photos
ranking_table.what_it_means: When people ask Google Photos questions in regular everyday language (like 'show me our picnic last year'), the AI often misinterprets what they mean, shows completely unrelated pictures, or guesses wrong.
ranking_table.why_it_is_important: Users expect conversational AI to act like a helpful assistant. When it guesses wrong or shows random photos, users lose confidence and stop using AI search.

ranking_table.title: Opportunity #3: Searching by Seasons & Milestones vs. Exact Dates
ranking_table.what_it_means: People remember roughly when things happened (like 'two summers ago' or 'around graduation'), but search often only works if you type the exact calendar month and year (like 'July 2022').
ranking_table.why_it_is_important: Forgetting the exact calendar date is the most common reason people struggle to find old photos. Search shouldn't fail just because someone doesn't remember the exact month.

ranking_table.title: Opportunity #4: Dead-End Screens When a Search Finds No Photos
ranking_table.what_it_means: When a search returns zero photos, the app shows a completely blank screen with no tips on what to try next, leaving users stuck having to scroll through years of photos by hand.
ranking_table.why_it_is_important: Endless manual scrolling through thousands of photos is the number one reason people get frustrated and close the app.

ranking_table.title: Opportunity #5: Telling Similar-Looking Photos Apart in Search Results
ranking_table.what_it_means: Search results show a dense grid of tiny, identical-looking picture squares with no dates or locations, making it exhausting to find the specific shot you actually wanted.
ranking_table.why_it_is_important: Finding candidate photos is useless if users have to tap into dozens of lookalike pictures one by one just to check which one is the right memory.

opportunities.title: Opportunity #1: Combining Multiple Details (Person + Place + Time)
opportunities.pain_point: When users combine multiple clues (like 'dad cooking at the beach house last summer'), search often chokes—showing zero results or matching only one word while ignoring the rest.
opportunities.opportunity: Make multi-detail search truly reliable by connecting people, locations, and time together without dropping words or showing blank screens.

opportunities.title: Opportunity #2: Natural-Language Questions Misread by Ask Photos
opportunities.pain_point: When users ask conversational questions to find memories, the AI frequently misinterprets their intent, returns random unrelated photos, or makes up answers.
opportunities.opportunity: Ensure AI search accurately understands everyday conversational phrasing and reliably matches the real moments in the user's photo collection.

opportunities.title: Opportunity #3: Searching by Seasons & Milestones vs. Exact Dates
opportunities.pain_point: Users remember seasons, holidays, and milestones ('last fall', 'around graduation'), but search fails unless they know the exact calendar month or date.
opportunities.opportunity: Support everyday time expressions (like seasons, approximate years, and holiday periods) so users can find photos without having to guess exact calendar dates.

opportunities.title: Opportunity #4: Dead-End Screens When a Search Finds No Photos
opportunities.pain_point: When a search brings up zero results, users hit a blank dead-end screen with no guidance or hints on how to rephrase, forcing them into exhausting manual timeline scrolling.
opportunities.opportunity: Provide helpful one-tap suggestions when a search comes up empty (such as 'Try a wider date range' or 'Show all photos with people') so users stay in the search flow.

opportunities.title: Opportunity #5: Telling Similar-Looking Photos Apart in Search Results
opportunities.pain_point: Search shows a dense wall of tiny, identical thumbnails with no dates, places, or clues showing why each photo matched, making target verification tiring.
opportunities.opportunity: Show clear date and location labels on search results so users can quickly recognize the exact memory they are looking for without having to open every photo.

opportunities.title: Saved screenshots and internet memes clogging photo searches
opportunities.pain_point: When users search for personal memories (like a family trip or birthday), search results get cluttered with forwarded WhatsApp memes, receipts, and screenshots.
opportunities.opportunity: Keep saved screenshots and downloaded memes distinct from camera photos so AI search focuses on personal life moments and loved ones.
